name: Adawat Tools: Prayer Times & Hijri Date – أدوات
author: mnsarl

sections.description:
A lightweight Arabic (RTL) plugin by adawat.org. It adds four ready-made widgets through simple shortcodes that work in the block editor (inside a Shortcode block), the classic editor and text widgets:

  • [adawat_hijri_date] — today’s Hijri date in the Umm al-Qura calendar, computed locally on your server from the full Umm al-Qura month table (1300–1600 AH) in your site’s timezone — no external requests, no JavaScript. Add gregorian="yes" to also show the matching Gregorian date.
  • [adawat_prayer_times city="riyadh"] — today’s prayer times for any of 188 cities, with a live next-prayer countdown. Times are computed astronomically in the visitor’s browser through the adawat.org widget — no API keys, no accounts. Options: method (mkk, egy, mwl, …), asr (1 standard, 2 Hanafi) and theme.
  • [adawat_ramadan_countdown] — days and hours left until Ramadan; event="fitr|adha|arafah|hijri" covers Eid al-Fitr, Eid al-Adha, Arafah day and the Hijri new year.
  • [adawat_zakat] — a mini zakat calculator (2.5% with the gold nisab); gold sets the gold gram price and cur the currency label.

From Settings → أدوات you choose the default city and theme (auto / light / dark) for all widgets at once, and theme="light|dark" on any shortcode overrides it.

Every widget renders a small “مدعوم من أدوات” credit line linking to the matching adawat.org tool page; you can switch it off on the settings page.

Privacy

  • [adawat_hijri_date] runs entirely on your server and never contacts any external service.
  • The other shortcodes embed an iframe from adawat.org; the visitor’s browser loads the widget from there like any normal iframe (the visitor’s IP reaches adawat.org as a standard web request). The widgets use no accounts and no ad tracking, and prayer times are computed inside the visitor’s own browser.

بالعربية

إضافة عربية خفيفة من موقع أدوات تضيف لموقعك أربع ودجات جاهزة عبر شورت كودات بسيطة: التاريخ الهجري بتقويم أم القرى (محسوب على خادمك بدون أي طلب خارجي)، ومواقيت الصلاة لـ188 مدينة مع عدّاد للصلاة القادمة، وعدّاد رمضان والأعياد، وحاسبة زكاة المال. تعمل في محرر المكوّنات والمحرر الكلاسيكي وودجات النص. التفاصيل الكاملة بالإنجليزية فوق.
sections.installation:
1. In your dashboard go to Plugins → Add New, search for “Adawat Tools”, or upload the ZIP from Upload Plugin.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. Open Settings → أدوات and pick the default city and theme.
  4. Put any shortcode in a post, a page or a text widget, for example: [adawat_prayer_times city="makkah" theme="dark"].
sections.faq:
Where do city slugs like riyadh and makkah come from?

They are the same identifiers used by the city pages on adawat.org: the URL https://adawat.org/prayer-times-riyadh.html means the slug is riyadh. The full list of all 188 cities is in the dropdown on Settings → أدوات, and you can also pass the Arabic name directly, for example city="جدة".

Does the Hijri date need an internet connection?

No. [adawat_hijri_date] is computed in PHP on your own server from the bundled Umm al-Qura month table (1300–1600 AH / 1882–2174 CE) — the same Umm al-Qura data that ICU ships and that adawat.org itself uses.

Does the conversion match the official Umm al-Qura calendar?

Yes, within the range of the table (1300–1600 AH). The conversion was tested automatically against the islamic-umalqura calendar in ICU over thousands of random dates and matched every one of them day for day.

Which prayer time calculation methods are supported?

Through the method attribute: Umm al-Qura mkk, Egyptian General Authority egy, Muslim World League mwl, Karachi kar, Jordan jo, ISNA isna, Dubai and the Gulf dub, Kuwait kw, Qatar qa, Morocco ma, South East Asia sea, France fr. If you do not set one, the official method of the city’s country is used automatically. For the Hanafi Asr add asr="2".

Can the “مدعوم من أدوات” credit line be hidden?

Yes. Turn the option off on Settings → أدوات, or do it in code with the adawat_tools_show_credit filter.

Does it work on non-Arabic (LTR) sites?

Yes. The widgets are self-contained RTL iframes and the Hijri date is plain text, so they render correctly on any site regardless of the theme’s language or direction.
sections.changelog:
1.0.0

  • First release: Hijri date shortcode (local Umm al-Qura port in PHP), prayer times for 188 cities, Ramadan countdown, zakat calculator.
  • Settings page: default city, light/dark theme, credit line toggle.
  • Sandboxed iframe embeds that resize themselves automatically and load lazily.
